rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim, Yaʿqūb, and a report from ʿAlī read with the tāʾ vowelled as the mother’s speech; others read it as God’s speech, supported by “God knows best what she bore.”
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم ويعقوب بما وضعت بضم التاء وروي عن علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥarrar can mean freed from servitude, or purified and corrected as a text is when edited.
rows.anchor: معنى المحرر في اللغة يحتمل أمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To accept is to receive something willingly; its root sense is reciprocation, as in accepting a gift.
rows.anchor: والتقبل أخذ الشيء على الرضا به كتقبل الهدية وأصل التقبل المقابلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waḍʿ means putting down; a woman’s putting down her child means giving birth, and related forms mean place, lowliness, or easing one’s pace.
rows.anchor: وأصل الوضع الحط وضعت المرأة الولد بمعنى ولدت

rows.speaker: الأخفش والمبرد
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash and al-Mubarrad parse idh as an object governed by an implied remember.
rows.anchor: أنه نصب بأذكر عن الأخفش والمبرد

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj connects idh to God’s choosing the family of ʿImrān.
rows.anchor: أنه متعلق باصطفى آل عمران عن الزجاج

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā connects idh to the attributes All-Hearing and All-Knowing, whose sense encompasses her speech and intention.
rows.anchor: أنه متعلق بسميع عليم فيعمل فيه معنى الصفتين تقديره والله مدرك لقولها ونيتها إذ قالت عن علي بن عيسى

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda treats idh as extra and unparsed; the author notes that Basran grammarians consider this wrong.
rows.anchor: أن إذ زائدة فلا موضع لها من الإعراب عن أبي عبيدة وهذا خطأ عند البصريين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥarraran is a circumstantial accusative describing what was in her womb, governed by her vow.
rows.anchor: ومحررا نصب على الحال من ما وتقديره نذرت لك الذي في بطني محررا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unthā is parsed as a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: وقوله { أنثى } نصب على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wife of ʿImrān is named Ḥanna, Mary’s grandmother; authorities differ whether her husband was ʿImrān ibn al-Hāshim or ʿImrān ibn Māthān, not Moses’ father, who lived eighteen centuries earlier.
rows.anchor: واسمها حنة جدة عيسى وكانتا أختين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Muqātil identify ʿImrān as Ibn Māthān and say the two sisters married ʿImrān and Zechariah; Yaḥyā and Mary were maternal cousins.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو عمران بن ماثان عن ابن عباس ومقاتل وليس بعمران أبي موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥanna obligates herself to dedicate the child in her womb to God’s service.
rows.anchor: أي أوجبت لك بأن أجعل ما في بطني

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid understands the vow as dedicating the child to serve the sanctuary and its places of worship.
rows.anchor: أي خادما للبيعة يخدم في متعبداتنا عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says the child was freed for worship and devoted exclusively to it.
rows.anchor: محررا للعبادة مخلصا لها عن الشعبي

rows.speaker: محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr says the child was freed for obedience to God, not used for personal benefits or needs.
rows.anchor: عتيقا خالصا لطاعتك لا استعمله في منافعي ولا أصرفه في الحوائج عن محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those dedicated to the sanctuary served and cleaned it until puberty, then could stay or leave.
rows.anchor: وكان المحرر إذا حرر جعل في الكنيسة يقوم عليها ويكنسها ويخدمها

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They say Ḥanna had despaired of having a child; seeing a bird feed its chick under a tree stirred her desire, so she prayed and conceived Mary.
rows.anchor: قالوا وكانت حنة قد أمسك عنها الولد حتى أيست فبينا هي تحت شجرة إذ رأت طائرا يزق فرخا له

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh reports that God told ʿImrān he would receive a blessed son who would heal the blind and leper, raise the dead by God’s leave, and be a messenger; Ḥanna then vowed her child.
rows.anchor: روي عن أبي عبد الله قال أوحى الله تعالى إلى عمران إني واهب لك ذكرا مباركا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥanna asks God to accept her vow with approval; He hears her words and knows her intention, which grounds her confidence.
rows.anchor: أي نذري قبول رضا { إنك أنت السميع } لما أقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says ʿImrān died while Ḥanna was pregnant; she delivered Mary, having hoped for a boy, and felt embarrassed.
rows.anchor: قيل إن عمران هلك وهي حامل فوضعت بعد ذلك يعني ولدت مريم وكانت ترجو أن يكون غلاما

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation is that she apologizes for being unable to fulfill the vow as intended because the child is female.
rows.anchor: وقيل فيه قولان أحدهما: أن المراد به الاعتذار من العدول عن النذر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The other explanation is that she foregrounds Mary’s being female to plead for her, since her capacity and strength are lower.
rows.anchor: والآخر: أن المراد تقديم الذكر في السؤال لها بأنها أنثى لأن سعيها أضعف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says He knows best what she bore because He created and formed her; under the alternate reading, Ḥanna says God knows better than she does.
rows.anchor: إخبار منه تعالى بأنه أعلم بوضعها لأنه هو الذي خلقها وصورها وعلى القراءة الأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A girl could not perform the male sanctuary service because menstruation and postpartum bleeding interrupted it and she needed protection from public display.
rows.anchor: لأنها لا تصلح لما يصلح له الذكر من التحرير لخدمة بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says custom permitted dedication only of boys.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة لم يكن التحرير إلا في الغلمان فيما جرت به العادة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the statement generally: males are superior to females and more suitable for tasks.
rows.anchor: وقيل أرادت أن الذكر أفضل من الأنثى على العموم وأصلح للأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in waḍaʿathā can refer back to mā fī baṭnī because mā can denote a feminine referent, or to something understood from context.
rows.anchor: والهاء في قوله وضعتها كناية عن ما في قوله ما في بطني وجاز ذلك لوقوع ما على مؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maryam is said in her language to mean worshipper or servant; Mary was the foremost and noblest woman of her time.
rows.anchor: وهي بلغتهم العابدة والخادمة فيما قيل وكانت مريم أفضل النساء في وقتها وأجلهن

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī transmits from Abū Hurayra that the Prophet named four women as sufficient examples of the world’s best: Mary, Āsiya, Khadīja, and Fāṭima.
rows.anchor: روى الثعلبي بإسناده عن أبي هريرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥanna fears the afflictions that commonly affect women and therefore seeks God’s protection for Mary and her descendants.
rows.anchor: خافت عليها ما يغلب على النساء من الآفات فقالت ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A prophetic report from Abū Hurayra says Satan touches every newborn at birth, causing its first cry, except Mary and her son; God protected them from that touch.
rows.anchor: فقد روى أبو هريرة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Ḥanna sought refuge for Mary and her descendants from Satan’s misguidance.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنها استعاذت من إغواء الشيطان الرجيم إياها عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufans read kaffalahā with a doubled fāʾ and others with a light fāʾ; the light form is supported by 3:44, where the guardianship is attributed to its subject.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة كفلها بالتشديد والباقون بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufans except Abū Bakr read the name in its shortened form; others lengthen it. Abū Bakr alone uses accusative with the long form; others use nominative.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة إلا أبا بكر زكريا مقصورا والباقون بالمد

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains the light reading through 3:44, where the guardianship verb is active and its subject is the one who takes Mary into care; doubling makes the Lord the subject and Zechariah the object.
rows.anchor: حجة من خفف كفلها قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name is read with shortening by Kūfans other than Abū Bakr and with lengthening by the other readers.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة إلا أبا بكر زكريا مقصورا والباقون بالمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal noun qabūl is used instead of taqabbul because the verb carries the sense of accepting, just as takarrum takes karam because it means being generous.
rows.anchor: إنما جاء مصدر تقبلها على القبول دون التقبل لأن فيه معنى قبلها

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr says qabūl with fatḥa has no parallel among verbal nouns, whose normal pattern has ḍamma.
rows.anchor: ولا نظير لقبول في المصادر بفتح فاء الفعل

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh lists five verbal nouns on the open fuʿūl pattern: qabūl, wuḍūʾ, ẓuhūr, wulūgh, and waqūd, though waqūd is usually closed when it is a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: جاءت خمسة مصادر على فعول بالفتح قبول ووضوء وظهور

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj permits qabūl with ḍamma and explains qabīl as a guarantor or surety.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الزجاج في قبول الضم والقبيل الكفيل وهو الضامن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kafala forms include kafaltuhu, akfuluhu, kaflan, kufūlan, and kafālan; a kāfil undertakes someone’s expenses and care.
rows.anchor: يقال كفلته أكفله كفلا وكفولا وكفالا فأنا كافل إذا تكفلت مؤنته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In legal terminology the one whose debt is guaranteed owes it, the beneficiary is owed it, the guaranteed thing is the debt, and the guarantor becomes liable.
rows.anchor: والمكفول عنه في الفقه هو الذي عليه الدين والمكفول له هو الذي له الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited report calls the Prophet the best one to be cared for in childhood and raised until maturity.
rows.anchor: أحق من كفل في صغره وأرضع حتى نشأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miḥrāb is the imam’s place in a mosque and originally the most honored, elevated place in an assembly; al-Zajjāj calls it a lofty, noble place.
rows.anchor: والمحراب مقام الإمام من المسجد وأصله أكرم موضع في المجلس وأشرفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poem uses miḥrāb for a high place reached by a ladder.
rows.anchor: لم ألقها أو أرتقي سلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepted Mary despite her being female, approving Ḥanna’s vow to dedicate her to service in the Jerusalem sanctuary, where no female had previously been accepted for this purpose.
rows.anchor: مع أنوثتها ورضي بها في النذر الذي نذرته حنة للعبادة في بيت المقدس ولم يقبل قبلها أنثى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets the acceptance as God taking charge of Mary’s upbringing and affairs.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه تكفل بها في تربيتها والقيام بشأنها عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says she never suffered illness at any time, day or night.
rows.anchor: وقبوله إياها أنه ما عرتها علة ساعة من ليل أو نهار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the good acceptance as God setting her on the path of the blessed.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه سلك بها طريق السعداء عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave Mary good growth and a sound form.
rows.anchor: { وأنبتها نباتا حسنا } أي جعل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says she grew in one day as much as another person grows in a year.
rows.anchor: وقيل سوى خلقها فكانت تنبت في يوم ما ينبت غيرها في عام عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says God supplied her with nourishment until she became a fully grown woman.
rows.anchor: بالغة تامة عن ابن جريج

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that at nine Mary fasted by day, prayed at night, and devoted herself to worship until she surpassed the scholars.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لما بلغت تسع سنين صامت النهار وقامت الليل وتبتلت حتى غلبت الأحبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the doubled reading God assigns Mary to Zechariah, who becomes her guardian; with the light reading Zechariah takes her into his care and undertakes her affairs.
rows.anchor: بالتشديد معناه ضمها الله إلى زكريا وجعله كفيلها

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق وجماعة
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq and others say Mary’s mother brought her wrapped to the sanctuary; priests competed for her, and Zechariah claimed priority because her aunt was his wife. They decided to draw lots among twenty-nine men.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق وجماعة وقيل بل ثبت قلم زكريا

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق وجماعة
rows.claim: In Ibn Isḥāq’s account, the pens were cast into flowing water; Zechariah’s stood upright above the water while the others sank, so he won.
rows.anchor: فألقوا أقلامهم في الماء فارتز قلم زكريا وارتفع فوق الماء ورسبت أقلامهم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī gives another sign: Zechariah’s pen stood up as if in clay, while the others were swept along with the current.
rows.anchor: عن السدي فسهمهم زكريا وقرعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah won the lot and was head of the priests and their prophet.
rows.anchor: فسهمهم زكريا وقرعهم وكان رأس الأحبار ونبيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lot account concludes by identifying Zechariah as the one who took Mary into his care.
rows.anchor: فذلك قوله { وكفلها زكريا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miḥrāb also means a mosque; another proposed etymology links it to war because Satan is fought there.
rows.anchor: ويقال للمسجد أيضا محراب ومنه ما يشاء من محاريب أي مساجد

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq says Zechariah first placed Mary with his wife, her maternal aunt; when Mary reached puberty, he built her a secluded upper room in the sanctuary, accessible only by a ladder, and brought her supplies daily.
rows.anchor: فقال محمد بن إسحاق ضمها إلى خالتها أم يحيى حتى إذا شبت وبلغت مبلغ النساء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, Mujāhid, and al-Suddī say Zechariah found fresh summer fruit with Mary in winter and winter fruit in summer.
rows.anchor: غضا طريا عن ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد والسدي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Mary was never nursed and her provision came from Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنها لم ترضع قط وإنما كان يأتيها رزقها من الجنة عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah asks in astonishment how and from where she obtained this provision.
rows.anchor: يعني قال لها زكريا كيف لك ومن أين لك هذا كالمتعجب منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary says the provision is from God, that is, from Paradise; the extraordinary gift honors her.
rows.anchor: أي من الجنة وهذه تكرمة من الله تعالى لها وإن كان ذلك خارقا للعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author holds that extraordinary signs may appear through people who are not prophets, including the saints.
rows.anchor: فإن عندنا يجوز أن تظهر الآيات الخارقة للعادة على غير الأنبياء والأصفياء

rows.speaker: البلخي
rows.claim: Al-Balkhī, representing those Muʿtazilites who deny miracles for non-prophets, says the provision established Jesus’ prophethood.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أن ذلك كان تأسيسا لنبوة عيسى عن البلخي

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says the provision came through Zechariah’s prayer and was therefore his miracle.
rows.anchor: والآخر: أنه كان بدعاء زكريا لها بالرزق في الجملة وكانت معجزة له عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Mary’s statement continues through “without reckoning,” it means God gives freely without payment earned by works; alternatively, God’s statement begins anew.
rows.anchor: ووجه اتصالها بما تقدم أن يكون حكاية لقول مريم وعلى هذا يكون معنى قوله بغير حساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anbāʾ is the plural of nabaʾ, meaning reports or news.
rows.anchor: الأنباء الأخبار الواحد نبأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waḥy is conveying a meaning secretly; it can mean God sending an angel to a prophet or inspiration, as in the revelation to the bee.
rows.anchor: والإيحاء هو إلقاء المعنى إلى الغير على وجه يخفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waḥy can also mean a gesture or signal, as when the people were signaled to glorify God morning and evening.
rows.anchor:
والإيحاء: الإيماء قال:
فأوحت إلينا

rows.speaker: العجاج
rows.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj uses waḥy for settling or conveying a quiet direction, in a line about something settling and being held firm.
rows.anchor:
قال العجاج:
أوحى لها القرار فاستقرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed poetic line uses waḥy for a gesture sent through fingers.
rows.anchor:
قال:
فأوحت إلينا والأنامل رسلها

rows.speaker: رؤبة
rows.claim: Ruʾba uses waḥy for writing, including writing in the scrolls of the Lord.
rows.anchor:
قال رؤبة:
لقدر كان وحاه الواحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qalam can mean a writing pen, a lottery arrow, or each person’s own allotted arrow; its root sense is cutting off an end.
rows.anchor: والقلم الذي يكتب به والقلم الذي يجال بين القوم كل إنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qalam also means trimming nails, while the joints of a spear are maqālim; both relate to cutting.
rows.anchor: والقلم قص الظفر ومقالم الرمح كعوبه وأصله قطع طرف الشيء

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī connects the first idh to “you were not”; the second may connect to “they were disputing,” or be a substitute for the first if both events coincided.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي إذ في قوله إذ يلقون متعلق بكنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhālika refers to the preceding account of Mary, Zechariah, and John.
rows.anchor: { ذلك } اشارة إلى ما تقدم ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God conveys the unseen account to Muḥammad as a proof, reminder, illumination, admonition, and lesson.
rows.anchor: أي نلقيه عليك معجزة وتذكيرا وتبصرة وموعظة وعبرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account demonstrates prophethood: Muḥammad had not witnessed these events or learned them from books, and his Meccan audience were not scriptural scholars.
rows.anchor: بين أهل مكة ولم يكونوا أهل كتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pens they cast may be the writing implements with which they wrote the Torah.
rows.anchor: أقلامهم } التي كانوا يكتبون بها التوراة في الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the objects were lottery arrows marked so they could determine who would care for Mary.
rows.anchor: وقيل أقلامهم أقداحهم للاقتراع جعلوا عليها علامات يعرفون بها من يكفل مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause omits an understood purpose: they cast lots to see whose lot would appear and who would care for Mary.
rows.anchor: وفيه حذف أي لينظروا أيهم تظهر قرعته ليكفل مريم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda reads the verse as expressing God’s amazement at how eagerly they sought to care for Mary.
rows.anchor: وهذا تعجيب من الله نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم من شدة حرصهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes it as amazement that they contested responsibility during a severe crisis, until the best guardian, Zechariah, was chosen for her.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو تعجيب من تدافعهم لكفالتها لشدة الأزمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their dispute shows they had reached the point of openly contending over Mary’s care.
rows.anchor: فيه دلالة على أنهم قد بلغوا في التشاح عليها إلى حد الخصومة

rows.speaker: الأكثر
rows.claim: Most say the dispute occurred at Mary’s birth, when her mother brought her to the sanctuary and they contested who would raise her.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: حين ولادتها وحمل أمها إلى الكنيسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes that casting lots can distinguish competing rights; the author cites sayings from al-Ṣādiq and al-Bāqir in support.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على أن للقرعة مدخلا في تميز الحقوق

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some date the dispute to Mary’s adulthood, when Zechariah could no longer raise her.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم كان ذلك وقت كبرها وعجز زكريا عن تربيتها

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says that when people delegate their matter to God and draw lots, the rightful person’s lot emerges; he calls such a decision just.
rows.anchor: قال الصادق ع: ما تقارع قوم

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Ṣādiq invokes the Qurʾānic case of Jonah, who drew lots and was among the defeated, as evidence for the practice.
rows.anchor: وقال: أي قضية أعدل من القرعة

rows.speaker: الباقر
rows.claim: Al-Bāqir says Mary was the first subject of a lot, followed by Jonah; he then recounts ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib’s lots over sacrificing his son ʿAbd Allāh, finally resolved by one hundred camels and three repeated draws.
rows.anchor: وقال الباقر: أول من سوهم عليه مريم ابنة عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads yabghūna in third person and turjaʿūna in second person; Ibn ʿAbbās, Ḥafṣ, Yaʿqūb, and Sahl use third person for both; the others use second person for both.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو يبغون بالياء وإليه ترجعون بالتاء مضمومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Second-person readings fit the address to the Prophet at the start; third person supplies an implied “tell them” and treats the people as absent.
rows.anchor: من قرأ بالتاء فيهما فلأن أول الآية خطاب للنبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening is a complete question; the fāʾ orders it as a response after the preceding signs: after all this, do they seek another religion?
rows.anchor: أفغير دين الله يبغون على جملة كما لو قيل أو غير دين الله يبغون إلا أن الفاء رتبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭawʿan and karhan are circumstantial accusatives meaning willingly and unwillingly, like “he came running” meaning that he came while running.
rows.anchor: وطوعا وكرها مصدران وقعا موقع الحال وتقديره طائعين وكارهين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that scriptural communities disputed before the Prophet about Abraham’s religion, each claiming priority; when he declared both groups dissociated from Abraham’s religion, they angrily rejected his judgment, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor:
عن ابن عباس قال
" اختصم أهل الكتاب إلى رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After showing Judaism and other religions false, God says that anyone seeking a religion other than His is astray and cannot be accepted.
rows.anchor: لما بين سبحانه بطلان اليهودية وسائر الملل غير الإسلام بين عقيبه أن من يبتغ غير دينه فهو ضال

words: وَلَهُ أَسْلَمَ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says creation submits through its state, which speaks and points to God, as at the covenant.
rows.anchor: أن معناه أسلم من في السماوات والأرض بحاله الناطقة عنه الدالة عليه عند أخذ الميثاق عليه عن ابن عباس

words: وَلَهُ أَسْلَمَ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: مجاهد وأبو العالية
rows.claim: Mujāhid and Abū al-ʿĀliya say submission means acknowledging God’s lordship, even among people who worship idols; reason directs creatures to confess their Creator.
rows.anchor: من الدلالة عن مجاهد وأبي العالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view says believers submit willingly, while disbelievers submit unwillingly at death.
rows.anchor: أسلم المؤمن طوعا وكرها والكافر كرها عند موته

rows.speaker: الكسائي والفراء
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ say the lām means “that” and marks the future required after verbs such as “I ordered” and “I wanted”; lām may be paired with kay to reinforce futurity.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الكسائي والفراء

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj rejects treating the lām as “that,” arguing that if it had that meaning it could not precede kay; he cites a verse using both.
rows.anchor: أردت لكيما يعلم الناس أنها

rows.speaker: سيبويه وأصحابه
rows.claim: Sībawayh and his school parse the lām with an implied verbal noun: God wants the clarification, paralleling expressions meaning “your interpretation of the dream” and “their fear of their Lord.”
rows.anchor: ومذهب سيبويه وأصحابه إن اللام دخلت هنا على تقدير المصدر أي لإرادة البيان

rows.speaker: كثير
rows.claim: Kathīr’s line exemplifies the verbal-noun reading: “I want forgetting her,” while her image appears along every path.
rows.anchor:
قال كثير:
أريد لأنسى ذكرها فكأنما

rows.speaker: بعض النحويين
rows.claim: Some grammarians object that the lām-as-“that” analysis lacks decisive proof, while the verbal-noun analysis seems to license an otherwise invalid delayed object; they allow it only when fronted.
rows.anchor: والقول الثالث: إن بعض النحويين ضعف هذين الوجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proposed constructions paraphrase “followed you,” “wants for you,” and “ordered us to submit” by supplying an implied clause or noun.
rows.anchor: فأما ردف لكم فعلى تأويل ردف ما ردف لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the competing analyses as unsettled and prefers an omitted object: God wants to give you guidance so that He may clarify.
rows.anchor: أن مفعول يريد محذوف تقديره يريد الله تبصيركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After explaining what is lawful and forbidden, God clarifies the rules of religion, worldly affairs, livelihood, and the hereafter for people’s benefit.
rows.anchor: ثم بين تعالى بعد التحليل والتحريم أنه يريد بذلك مصالحنا ومنافعنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says God guides people to the paths of both righteous and wicked predecessors so they may follow their examples.
rows.anchor: يهديكم إلى طريق الذين كانوا من قبلكم من أهل الحق والباطل لتكونوا مقتدين بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says knowledge of earlier people’s ways gives insight into what to practice and avoid.
rows.anchor: لتكونوا على بصيرة فيما تفعلون وتجتنبون من طرائقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepts repentance, or wills repentance for people by calling and urging them toward it and making its path accessible.
rows.anchor: أي ويقبل توبتكم. ويقال: يريد التوبة عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse disproves the Mujabira position because God says He wills only what is good and beneficial.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على بطلان مذهب المجبرة لأنه بين تعالى أنه لا يريد إلا الخير والصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God wills to show grace toward people’s repentance if it occurs; another explanation is that He grants success and strengthens their motives to repent.
rows.anchor: أي يلطف في توبتكم أن وقع منك ذلك. وقيل: يريد أن يوفقكم لها

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the phrase concerns all people of falsehood, since every false claimant follows personal desire; the author considers this the closest view.
rows.anchor: أن المعنى بذلك جميع المبطلين فإن كل مبطل متبع شهوة نفسه في باطله عن ابن زيد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid identifies those following desires as adulterers.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بذلك الزناة عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī identifies them as Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: أنهم اليهود والنصارى عن السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth view identifies them specifically as Jews, who claimed that the paternal half-sister was lawful in the Torah.
rows.anchor: ورابعها: أنهم اليهود خاصة إذ قالوا: إن الأخت من الأب حلال في التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A great deviation means plainly departing from uprightness through abundant sin; uprightness leads to reward and safety from punishment, while deviation leads to ruin and punishment.
rows.anchor: أي تعدلوا عن الاستقامة عدولا بينا بالاستكثار من المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating that God wills repentance emphasizes the point: the first statement promises guidance and return, the second contrasts God’s will with the desires of people of passion.
rows.anchor: فجوابه أنه للتأكيد، وأيضا فإن في الأول بيان أنه يريد الهداية والإنابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second occurrence adds an, removing ambiguity: God wants people to repent, not merely wants to do so without intending their repentance.
rows.anchor: وأيضا أنه أتي في الثاني بأن ليزول الإبهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sinners take comfort in sharing sin with others, just as the obedient find affinity with the obedient; sinners want company in wrongdoing to avoid blame and reproach.
rows.anchor: لأن العاصي يأنس بالعاصي كما يأنس المطيع بالمطيع

rows.speaker: مجاهد وطاوس
rows.claim: Mujāhid and Ṭāwūs say God lightens the rules concerning women and marriage by permitting marriage to enslaved women.
rows.anchor: يعني في التكليف في أمر النساء والنكاح بإباحة نكاح الإماء عن مجاهد وطاوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lightening may refer to accepting repentance and enabling people to repent.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يريد التخفيف بقبول التوبة والتوفيق لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God lightens the general burden of religious obligations, giving this community less than earlier communities bore.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يريد التخفيف في التكليف على العموم وذلك أنه تعالى خفف عن هذه الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human weakness here concerns women: people have little patience in resisting them.
rows.anchor: في أمر النساء وقلة الصبر عنهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says people are weak because desire pulls them and fear and grief overwhelm them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: خلق الإنسان ضعيفا يستميله هواه وشهوته ويستشيطه خوفه وحزنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation is placed in the case of three Banū Ubairiq brothers: Bishr, Bashīr, and Mubashshir; Bashīr, called Abū Ṭuʿma, wrote satires against the Prophet’s companions and attributed them to others.
rows.anchor: نزلت في بني أبيرق وكانوا ثلاثة إخوة بشر وبشير ومبشر وكان بشير يكنى أبا طعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ṭuʿma broke into the upper room of Rifāʿa ibn Zayd and stole food, a sword, and armor; Rifāʿa complained to his nephew Qatāda ibn al-Nuʿmān.
rows.anchor: فنقب أبو طعمة على علية رفاعة بن زيد وأخذ له طعاما وسيفا ودرعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Qatāda and Rifāʿa investigated, the brothers blamed the theft on Labīd ibn Sahl; Labīd confronted them, accusing them of theft and hypocrisy and warning them to stop slandering the Prophet.
rows.anchor: فقال بنو أبيرق والله ما صاحبكم إلا لبيد بن سهل رجل ذو حسب ونسب

rows.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
rows.claim: Qatāda told the Prophet that a bad household had attacked his uncle and broken into his upper room, taking food and weapons; the Prophet first told him to investigate.
rows.anchor: وأتى قتادة رسول الله فقال يا رسول الله إن أهل بيت منا أهل بيت سوء عدوا على عمي

rows.speaker: أسير بن عروة
rows.claim: Usayr ibn ʿUrwa gathered men from the brothers’ clan and accused Qatāda and Rifāʿa of slandering a reputable, righteous household; after hearing him, the Prophet rebuked Qatāda when he returned.
rows.anchor: يقال له أسير بن عروة جمع رجالا من أهل الدار ثم انطلق إلى رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qatāda left wishing he had died rather than speak to the Prophet; Rifāʿa replied that God was the one to seek help from. The passage from this verse through “God does not forgive associating partners” was revealed.
rows.anchor: فقال عمه رفاعة الله المستعان فنزلت الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Bashīr learned that the Qurʾān had exposed him, he fled to Mecca and apostatized; he stayed with Sulāfa bt. Saʿd, whom Ḥassān satirized in a poem.
rows.anchor: فبلغ بشيرا ما نزل فيه من القرآن فهرب إلى مكة وارتد كافرا فنزل على سلافة بنت سعد
